properties.name: Wiley / Hindawi
properties.group: Big publishers that printed papers bought from paper mills, then retracted them
properties.type, as the page says: Major publisher hit by paper mills
properties.detail: After Wiley bought Hindawi (2021), paper mills flooded its special issues; Wiley retracted 11,300+ papers and had 19 journals delisted by Clarivate.
properties.note: Wiley discontinued the Hindawi brand in 2024; cleanup cost an estimated $35-40M.

properties.name: OMICS Publishing Group
properties.group: Publishers that take fees but skip real checking (predatory), fined or blacklisted
properties.detail: A US court ordered OMICS to pay $50.1M (2019) after the FTC proved deceptive practices: fake peer review, hidden fees, bogus impact factors and misused researcher names.
properties.note: The archetypal predatory publisher; also runs Allied Academies, Pulsus, iMedPub, Longdom.

properties.name: Cabells Predatory Reports
properties.group: Publishers that take fees but skip real checking (predatory), fined or blacklisted
properties.detail: The successor to Beall’s List; catalogues over 15,000 journals using deceptive or predatory practices.
properties.note: A catalogue, not one firm — a measure of the predatory long tail.

properties.name: IEEE
properties.group: Big publishers that printed papers bought from paper mills, then retracted them
properties.type, as the page says: Major publisher hit by paper mills
properties.detail: Has withdrawn thousands of substandard or fabricated conference papers from IEEE Xplore, including computer-generated (SCIgen) nonsense papers.
properties.note: The world's largest technical professional body; mostly a conference-proceedings problem.

properties.name: Springer Nature
properties.group: Big publishers that printed papers bought from paper mills, then retracted them
properties.type, as the page says: Major publisher hit by paper mills
properties.detail: Repeated mass retractions across BMC, the Arabian Journal of Geosciences and others for fake peer review and paper-mill content.
properties.note: A leading legitimate publisher; several journals were infiltrated and later purged.

properties.name: MDPI
properties.group: Journals publishing huge numbers of papers fast, criticised for weak checks (megajournals)
properties.detail: High-volume special-issue model; its IJERPH published ~17,000 papers in 2022; Clarivate delisted 2 MDPI titles and China's CAS put 22 on a warning list.
properties.note: MDPI rejects paper-mill claims and says delistings were on a 'content-relevance' criterion, not quality.

properties.name: Elsevier
properties.group: Big publishers that printed papers bought from paper mills, then retracted them
properties.type, as the page says: Major publisher hit by paper mills
properties.detail: Paper-mill-infiltrated special issues and fake peer review have triggered retractions across multiple Elsevier journals.
properties.note: The largest scientific publisher; targeted by mills like everyone else.

properties.name: Beall's-listed predatory publishers
properties.group: Publishers that take fees but skip real checking (predatory), fined or blacklisted
properties.detail: Beall's List and its successor lists catalogued well over 1,000 predatory open-access publishers and journals that charge fees with little or no real peer review.
properties.note: A category, not one firm; the long tail of pay-to-publish operations.

properties.name: WASET
properties.group: Fake or pay-to-present science conferences
properties.detail: The World Academy of Science, Engineering and Technology is widely flagged for predatory conferences and journals using copied names and fake metrics.
properties.note: Investigated by journalists across Europe (e.g. the 2018 'Fake Science' exposes).

properties.name: Frontiers
properties.group: Journals publishing huge numbers of papers fast, criticised for weak checks (megajournals)
properties.detail: Very high volume with heavy China exposure; once appeared on Beall's predatory list; criticised for pressure on editors. Cut output sharply after 2022.
properties.note: Frontiers disputes the predatory label; no mass-retraction event like Hindawi's.

properties.name: SCIRP (Scientific Research Publishing)
properties.group: Publishers that take fees but skip real checking (predatory), fined or blacklisted
properties.detail: Scientific Research Publishing has long appeared on predatory-publisher lists for weak review and aggressive fee-seeking.

properties.name: Taylor & Francis
properties.group: Big publishers that printed papers bought from paper mills, then retracted them
properties.type, as the page says: Major publisher hit by paper mills
properties.detail: Its journal Bioengineered was delisted by Clarivate after paper-mill activity, with 86+ retractions there alone.
properties.note: A major legitimate publisher with infiltrated titles.

properties.name: PLOS (PLOS ONE)
properties.group: Journals publishing huge numbers of papers fast, criticised for weak checks (megajournals)
properties.detail: PLOS ONE, long the world’s largest journal, has retracted hundreds of papers, many for image manipulation and integrity failures.
properties.note: A nonprofit open-access pioneer; sheer volume left a large cleanup.

properties.name: Scientific Reports (Springer Nature)
properties.group: Journals publishing huge numbers of papers fast, criticised for weak checks (megajournals)
properties.documented scale: World’s largest journal; hundreds of retractions
properties.detail: Publishes ~20,000 papers a year and has accumulated hundreds of retractions for manipulation and paper-mill content.

properties.name: e-Century Publishing
properties.group: Big publishers that printed papers bought from paper mills, then retracted them
properties.type, as the page says: Major publisher hit by paper mills
properties.detail: Its biomedical journals saw mass retractions for paper-mill and image-duplication content; several were delisted.

properties.name: Sage
properties.group: Big publishers that printed papers bought from paper mills, then retracted them
properties.type, as the page says: Major publisher hit by paper mills
properties.detail: Retracted 209 + 122 papers from one engineering journal for compromised peer review; earlier exposed a 2014 fake-peer-review ring.

properties.name: Bentham Open
properties.group: Publishers that take fees but skip real checking (predatory), fined or blacklisted
properties.detail: Subject of a famous 2009 sting when a deliberately nonsensical computer-generated paper was accepted.

properties.name: Allied Academies / Pulsus
properties.group: Publishers that take fees but skip real checking (predatory), fined or blacklisted
properties.detail: Acquired by OMICS; carries the same predatory journal and conference practices.

properties.name: Spandidos Publications
properties.group: Big publishers that printed papers bought from paper mills, then retracted them
properties.type, as the page says: Major publisher hit by paper mills
properties.detail: Greek biomedical publisher hit by waves of image-duplication retractions flagged by integrity sleuths.

properties.name: AME Publishing Company
properties.group: Big publishers that printed papers bought from paper mills, then retracted them
properties.type, as the page says: Major publisher hit by paper mills
properties.detail: Several AME journals were removed from Clarivate’s Web of Science in the 2023 purge.

properties.name: Science Publishing Group
properties.group: Publishers that take fees but skip real checking (predatory), fined or blacklisted
properties.detail: Open-access publisher long flagged for minimal review and deceptive metrics.

properties.name: David Publishing
properties.group: Publishers that take fees but skip real checking (predatory), fined or blacklisted
properties.detail: Mass solicitation and pay-to-publish journals across many fields.

properties.name: Academic Journals
properties.group: Publishers that take fees but skip real checking (predatory), fined or blacklisted
properties.detail: High-volume open-access publisher repeatedly listed as predatory.
